title: When the phone cannot count its own workouts, a restore treats the phone as empty and can replace everything without asking
what: Before a restore from a backup file, the phone counts what it already holds. If that count fails, the failure is swallowed and the phone is taken to be empty, so tapping Restore replaces everything at once with no 'Are you sure?' question. The Drive bring-back and its undo do the same with their counts: a failed count is shown as 'nothing is lost', so the question understates what goes.
expected: A failed count never reads as 'nothing here'. The member is still asked before anything is replaced, and the question says the phone's workouts could not be counted.
how_often: rare: only when the phone's own count fails
fix_line: When the count fails, still ask before replacing and say the phone's contents could not be counted

title: The 'finish your workout first' guard before a restore lets the restore go ahead if the open workout cannot be read
what: A restore must wait until an open workout is finished or discarded, because a restore breaks that workout so it can never be saved. Both restore cards first read the open workout; if that read fails, the error is swallowed (or only logged) and the restore goes ahead as if no workout were open.
expected: If the open workout cannot be read, the restore stops and asks the member to try again, rather than going ahead.
who: members restoring with a workout in progress
how_often: rare: only when reading the open workout fails
fix_line: Stop the restore with a try-again line when the open workout cannot be read

title: If the profile cannot be read, Edit profile shows blank locked boxes with no message
what: When reading the profile fails, the error is swallowed. The card shows empty boxes that cannot be typed in, still under the line 'Changes save as you go', with no 'Couldn't load' words or Try again. If only the saved mobile number fails to load, the number box shows empty as if none were saved.
expected: A failed read shows the app's own 'Couldn't load, try again' state instead of blank boxes.
how_often: rare: only when the phone's own data read fails
fix_line: Show the shared load-error state with Try again when the profile read fails

title: An unused choice-chips piece is left in the Stats parts
what: The Stats parts file still offers a one-of-many chips row that nothing in the app uses any more; the Settings chips have their own version.
expected: Unused pieces are removed so there is one chips row to keep right.

title: Settings and backup tests mostly look for words in the code, and one passes while the photo backup switch cannot be reached
what: Most tests that name the Settings cards (backup, restore, erase, account, join gym, profile, gym settings) read the file as text and check that a line or sentence is in it. One test 'proves' Settings offers the photo backup switch because the card's name is in the file, while no Settings row opens that page. 39 files in this area are imported by no test at all, among them the restore, erase, sign-in and confirm sheets.
expected: Tests call the logic the cards use or draw the card and check what the member sees, and the restore and erase cards have at least one test each.
fix_line: Replace word-in-file checks with checks of what the card does, starting with restore and erase
